## 0. What this notebook does differently

A variant of `DMS_analysis.Rmd` (see that notebook for the full walkthrough
- not repeated here). Section 3's library-complexity check there found a
handful of binders dominating the read counts in every sample, squeezing
everyone else. Since every binder's count is a *share* of a fixed total, a
binder's apparent frequency can shift just because the dominant clones'
share shifted, even if nothing real changed for that binder.

**The fix here**: split the panel into a high-expressing batch and a
low-expressing batch *before* normalising, and run the comparison
separately within each - low-expressing binders are never thrown out, just
compared only against others at a similar abundance.

```{r libraries}
library(tidyverse)
library(scales)
```

## 1. Load data

```{r load-data}
counts_long <- read_tsv("../results/binder_counts.tsv", show_col_types = FALSE)
samples     <- read_tsv("../config/samples_template.tsv", show_col_types = FALSE)

counts_long <- counts_long %>%
  complete(binder_id, sample_id = samples$sample_id, fill = list(count = 0)) %>%
  left_join(samples %>% select(sample_id, condition, ara_pct, iptg_mM),
            by = "sample_id")

head(counts_long)
```

One row per binder, one column per sample, once you reshape it - does this
match `config/samples_template.tsv`?

## 2. Library representation: plasmid pool vs. after growth

`plasmid_library` is the pooled plasmid prep itself - no transformation, no
growth, no selection at all. Comparing it to `no_inducer` (grown, plain
antibiotic selection, nothing induced) tells you whether any skew you see
later already existed in the tube, or only shows up once cells start
growing.

```{r plasmid-library-check}
plasmid_vs_no_inducer <- counts_long %>%
  filter(condition %in% c("plasmid_library", "no_inducer")) %>%
  group_by(sample_id) %>%
  mutate(freq = count / sum(count)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(binder_id, condition, freq) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = condition, values_from = freq)

plasmid_vs_no_inducer %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = plasmid_library, y = no_inducer)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40") +
  scale_x_log10(labels = label_number()) +
  scale_y_log10(labels = label_number()) +
  labs(x = "Relative frequency: plasmid_library", y = "Relative frequency: no_inducer",
       title = "Library representation: raw plasmid prep vs. after growth") +
  theme_minimal()
```

Does this look like fair representation, or does the library structure
already look skewed before a single cell was even grown? Worth an answer
before deciding the batch split below is even needed.

## 3. QC: sequencing depth, library complexity, viability

```{r qc-depth}
depth <- counts_long %>%
  group_by(sample_id, condition) %>%
  summarise(total_reads = sum(count), n_binders_detected = sum(count > 0), .groups = "drop")

depth %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = reorder(sample_id, total_reads), y = total_reads, fill = condition)) +
  geom_col() +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Total usable read pairs", title = "Sequencing depth per sample") +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r qc-table}
depth
```

A sample with much lower depth than the others deserves a second look - what
would you check?

### Library complexity: how evenly is the pool represented?

```{r library-complexity}
complexity <- counts_long %>%
  group_by(sample_id, condition) %>%
  mutate(sample_total = sum(count)) %>%
  arrange(sample_id, desc(count)) %>%
  mutate(rank = row_number(), cum_share = cumsum(count) / sample_total) %>%
  ungroup()

complexity %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = rank, y = cum_share, group = sample_id, colour = condition)) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.9, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40") +
  labs(x = "Binders, ranked by abundance (most abundant first)",
       y = "Cumulative share of reads",
       title = "Library complexity per sample",
       subtitle = "A steep early climb to the dashed line (90%) means a handful of binders dominate the pool") +
  theme_minimal()
```

Flat here? Splitting into batches won't change much - `DMS_analysis.Rmd`
alone would do.

### Viability filter: drop binders that don't survive no-inducer selection

```{r viability-filter}
min_no_inducer_reads <- 10  # tune by eye against the histogram below

no_inducer_counts <- counts_long %>%
  filter(condition == "no_inducer") %>%
  select(binder_id, no_inducer_count = count)

no_inducer_counts %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = no_inducer_count)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = min_no_inducer_reads, linetype = "dashed", colour = "red") +
  labs(x = "no_inducer read count", y = "Number of binders",
       title = "Choosing the viability threshold",
       subtitle = paste("Dashed line: current threshold =", min_no_inducer_reads)) +
  theme_minimal()

dead_binders <- no_inducer_counts %>%
  filter(no_inducer_count < min_no_inducer_reads) %>%
  pull(binder_id)

if (length(dead_binders) > 0) {
  cat(length(dead_binders), " binder(s) dropped as non-viable (no_inducer count < ",
      min_no_inducer_reads, "): ", paste(dead_binders, collapse = ", "), "\n", sep = "")
} else {
  cat("No binders dropped - all binders survive no-inducer selection above threshold.\n")
}

counts_long <- counts_long %>% filter(!(binder_id %in% dead_binders))
```

### Low-count filter: drop binders too thinly covered overall

```{r low-count-filter}
min_mean_count <- 5  # tune by eye against the histogram below

mean_counts <- counts_long %>%
  filter(condition != "plasmid_library") %>%  # not part of the downstream comparison
  group_by(binder_id) %>%
  summarise(mean_count = mean(count), .groups = "drop")

mean_counts %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = mean_count)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = min_mean_count, linetype = "dashed", colour = "red") +
  labs(x = "Mean read count across all samples", y = "Number of binders",
       title = "Choosing the low-count filter threshold",
       subtitle = paste("Dashed line: current threshold =", min_mean_count)) +
  theme_minimal()

low_count_binders <- mean_counts %>%
  filter(mean_count < min_mean_count) %>%
  pull(binder_id)

if (length(low_count_binders) > 0) {
  cat(length(low_count_binders), " binder(s) dropped for too few reads overall (mean count < ",
      min_mean_count, "): ", paste(low_count_binders, collapse = ", "), "\n", sep = "")
} else {
  cat("No binders dropped - all binders average at least ", min_mean_count, " reads across all samples.\n", sep = "")
}

counts_long <- counts_long %>% filter(!(binder_id %in% low_count_binders))
```

### Splitting into high- and low-expressing batches

Rank binders by overall abundance (mean count across all samples). At or
above the threshold -> high-expressing batch; everyone else -> low.

```{r expression-batch-split}
high_expr_threshold <- 1000  # mean read count across all samples; tune by eye against the histogram below

overall_abundance <- counts_long %>%
  filter(condition != "plasmid_library") %>%  # classify by dominance in the samples that matter downstream
  group_by(binder_id) %>%
  summarise(mean_count_overall = mean(count), .groups = "drop")

overall_abundance %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = mean_count_overall)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30) +
  scale_x_log10(labels = label_number()) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = high_expr_threshold, linetype = "dashed", colour = "red") +
  labs(x = "Mean read count across all samples (log scale)", y = "Number of binders",
       title = "Choosing the high/low expression split",
       subtitle = paste("Dashed line: current threshold =", high_expr_threshold)) +
  theme_minimal()

expr_batch <- overall_abundance %>%
  mutate(batch = if_else(mean_count_overall >= high_expr_threshold, "high", "low"))

high_expr_binders <- expr_batch %>% filter(batch == "high") %>% pull(binder_id)
low_expr_binders  <- expr_batch %>% filter(batch == "low") %>% pull(binder_id)

cat(length(high_expr_binders), " binder(s) assigned to the high-expressing batch, ",
    length(low_expr_binders), " to the low-expressing batch.\n", sep = "")

# The high batch should hold most of the READS; the low batch most of the
# BINDERS. That mismatch is the whole reason to split.
counts_long %>%
  left_join(expr_batch %>% select(binder_id, batch), by = "binder_id") %>%
  group_by(batch) %>%
  summarise(n_binders = n_distinct(binder_id), total_reads = sum(count), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(share_of_reads = total_reads / sum(total_reads))
```

Does the high batch look like a small handful of dominant clones, or a more
gradual spread? How would that change how much you trust the split?

## 4. The per-batch pipeline

Fitness here uses `DMS_analysis.Rmd`'s reference-binder approach - a
ratio-of-ratios relative to one binder you're confident isn't a hit, rather
than a plain frequency ratio (see that notebook's Section 6 for the
formula). One reference, picked once, used for both batches: the formula is
built from raw counts with no per-sample or per-batch total in it anywhere,
so it doesn't matter which batch the reference itself happens to land in.

Does the batch split still matter once fitness is computed this way, rather
than as a frequency? What is and isn't a frequency-only problem here?

```{r batch-pipeline-functions}
pseudocount <- 1
reference_binder <- "result_50aa_1_10"  # <- pick your own; same one for both batches

reference_counts <- counts_long %>%
  filter(binder_id == reference_binder, condition %in% c("library_only_0.1mM", "toxin_plus_library_0.1mM")) %>%
  select(condition, count) %>%
  deframe()
ref_input    <- reference_counts[["library_only_0.1mM"]]
ref_selected <- reference_counts[["toxin_plus_library_0.1mM"]]

run_batch_pipeline <- function(counts_batch) {
  counts_norm <- counts_batch %>%
    group_by(sample_id) %>%
    mutate(
      total_reads = sum(count),
      freq        = (count + pseudocount) / (total_reads + pseudocount * n_distinct(counts_batch$binder_id))
    ) %>%
    ungroup()

  condition_freq <- counts_norm %>%
    select(condition, binder_id, freq)

  baseline <- condition_freq %>%
    filter(condition == "no_inducer") %>%
    select(binder_id, baseline_freq = freq)

  innate_toxicity <- condition_freq %>%
    filter(condition == "library_only_0.1mM") %>%
    left_join(baseline, by = "binder_id") %>%
    mutate(log2FC = log2(freq / baseline_freq))

  p_innate_toxicity <- innate_toxicity %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = binder_id, y = log2FC)) +
    geom_col() +
    labs(x = "Binder", y = "log2FC vs. no_inducer",
         title = "Innate toxicity of overexpression (no toxin present)") +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_blank())

  key_comparison <- counts_batch %>%
    filter(condition %in% c("library_only_0.1mM", "toxin_plus_library_0.1mM")) %>%
    select(binder_id, condition, count) %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = condition, values_from = count) %>%
    rename(input = library_only_0.1mM, selected = toxin_plus_library_0.1mM) %>%
    mutate(
      fitness = log2((selected + pseudocount) / (input + pseudocount) /
                     ((ref_selected + pseudocount) / (ref_input + pseudocount)))
    )

  p_key_comparison <- key_comparison %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = reorder(binder_id, fitness), y = fitness)) +
    geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
    coord_flip() +
    labs(x = "Binder", y = "Fitness (relative to reference)",
         title = "Fitness: toxin+library vs. library-only (this batch only)") +
    theme_minimal()

  hit_results <- key_comparison %>%
    select(binder_id, fitness) %>%
    arrange(desc(fitness))

  p_final <- hit_results %>%
    slice_max(fitness, n = 20) %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = reorder(binder_id, fitness), y = fitness)) +
    geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
    coord_flip() +
    labs(x = "Binder", y = "Fitness (relative to reference)",
         title = "Top binders by protection (this batch only)") +
    theme_minimal()

  list(
    innate_toxicity = innate_toxicity, p_innate_toxicity = p_innate_toxicity,
    key_comparison = key_comparison, p_key_comparison = p_key_comparison,
    hit_results = hit_results, p_final = p_final
  )
}

compare_to_plate <- function(hit_results, plate_reference, batch_label) {
  binder_name_map <- tibble(binder_id = unique(hit_results$binder_id)) %>%
    mutate(
      genename = binder_id %>%
        str_remove("^rcat-binder-") %>%
        str_remove("^result_") %>%
        str_replace("_result_", "_")
    )

  comparison <- hit_results %>%
    left_join(binder_name_map, by = "binder_id") %>%
    left_join(plate_reference, by = "genename") %>%
    filter(!is.na(plate_log2_efsize))

  p <- comparison %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = plate_log2_efsize, y = fitness, colour = plate_hit)) +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.7, size = 2) +
    geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, colour = "grey40", linetype = "dashed") +
    labs(x = "Published plate assay: log2(effect size), Sen2 (vs. IPTG-low)",
         y = paste0(batch_label, "-batch fitness (toxin+library vs. library-only)"),
         title = paste0("This screen (", batch_label, " batch) vs. the published plate-based assay"),
         colour = "Plate-assay hit call") +
    theme_minimal()

  cor_summary <- comparison %>%
    summarise(
      pearson_r         = cor(fitness, plate_log2_efsize, use = "complete.obs"),
      n_binders_matched = n()
    ) %>%
    mutate(batch = batch_label, .before = 1)

  list(comparison = comparison, plot = p, cor_summary = cor_summary)
}
```

## 7. Comparing each batch to the published plate-based screen (Sen2 retron)

Same reference data and caveats as `DMS_analysis.Rmd` Section 8 - run once
per batch.

```{r load-plate-reference}
plate_reference <- read_tsv("../data/plate_assay_reference_hits.tsv", show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  filter(retron == "Sen2") %>%
  transmute(genename, plate_pval = pval, plate_log2_efsize = log2(efsize), plate_hit = hit)
```

```{r plate-compare-batches}
cmp_high <- compare_to_plate(high$hit_results, plate_reference, "high-expressing")
cmp_low  <- compare_to_plate(low$hit_results,  plate_reference, "low-expressing")

print(cmp_high$plot)
print(cmp_low$plot)

bind_rows(cmp_high$cor_summary, cmp_low$cor_summary)
```

```{r save-plate-comparisons}
write_csv(cmp_high$comparison, "../results/plate_assay_comparison_high.csv")
write_csv(cmp_low$comparison, "../results/plate_assay_comparison_low.csv")
```

## 8. Did splitting help?

Compare the table above against `DMS_analysis.Rmd`'s unsplit
`plate_assay_comparison.csv` correlation.

- Better here for the low-expressing batch? That points at the dominant
  clones distorting things for everyone else in the unsplit version.
- About the same? Read depth, not compositional squeeze, is the limit -
  something splitting can't fix.
- The high-expressing batch's correlation rests on very few points - how
  much would one outlier change it?

## Where to go from here

* If almost everything lands in one batch, `high_expr_threshold` in
  Section 3 needs moving - use the histogram, not a fixed number.
* This splits on overall abundance once, globally - a binder that's
  middling in one condition but dominant in another still gets assigned to
  a single batch for everything. Would a per-condition split change your
  answer?
* Everything in `DMS_analysis.Rmd`'s own "Where to go from here" applies
  here too.
